plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: An airy annual with feathery foliage and daisy-like flowers on tall slender stems. It thrives in full sun and poor soil, and in mild autumn regions it continues blooming until the first hard frost.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer to late autumn (Northern Hemisphere); spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to Mexico; widely cultivated in gardens across North America, Europe, Asia, and Australia
plants.funFact: Cosmos comes from the Greek word 'kosmos', meaning order or harmony. Cosmos seeds were even carried into space, and the plants have bloomed aboard the International Space Station.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A graceful subtropical tree that erupts in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, often before its fern-like leaves emerge. Blossoms carpet streets and lawns with purple when they fall.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; planted in Pretoria, Johannesburg, Sydney, Brisbane, Buenos Aires, and other subtropical cities
plants.funFact: Pretoria in South Africa is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its tens of thousands of jacaranda trees, which turn the streets purple every October.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum x morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in many forms, including pompon, spider, and decorative types. Short days trigger flowering, which makes it a hallmark of fall gardens and festivals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Originated in China; cultivated worldwide, especially in East Asia, Europe, and North America
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums have been cultivated in China for over 2,500 years, and in Japan the flower is the emblem of the Imperial family and is celebrated at the Chrysanthemum Festival.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped pink-lilac flowers in autumn with no leaves present. The strap-like foliage appears the following spring and dies back by summer.
plants.location: Native to damp meadows and woodlands in Europe from Britain to the Mediterranean; grown in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a true crocus. All parts are highly toxic because they contain colchicine, a compound that is also used in medicine and in plant breeding to double chromosome numbers.
